chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Water is the chief of drinks in this world and the Hereafter.

key_terms.الشَّرَابِ: Drinks, beverages — all forms of drinkable liquids
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter — the eschatological realm following death and resurrection
key_terms.سَيِّدُ: Chief, master, lord — the most excellent or preeminent of a category

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the importance of water in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) declared that water holds the highest rank among all beverages, both in this life and in the life to come. This statement reflects the Islamic understanding of water as the foundational blessing of creation — as the Quran states, 'We made every living thing from water' (21:30). The hadith would have resonated deeply with its early audience in the Arabian Peninsula, where water was a precious and life-sustaining resource, affirming that its primacy is not merely worldly but also spiritual and eschatological.
